Figure 1 illustrates OWC scenarios, including V2V and V2I communication, as well as a Fi-Wi-Fi bridge. The 6G-EWOC project aims to develop a 6G-V2X network that combines fiber-optic and wireless technologies with AI to support advanced network and CAM services. The project focuses on the development of OWC technologies for V2V and V2I communications, as well as the integration of C-V2X systems. The architecture includes a photonic lantern-based remote radio head for V2I OWC, a Fi-Wi-Fi bridge for fiber-scarce areas, and an AI-driven control and orchestration system for resource optimization.

The paper reports several performance metrics, including data rates of >100 Mb/s for V2V OWC and >1 Gb/s for V2I OWC. The Fi-Wi-Fi bridge is reported to have a loss of <13 dB for a 100 m link. The project aims to demonstrate 17 KPIs, including V2V and V2I data rates, user data rates, and energy efficiency. The reported metrics seem physically consistent, but further analysis is needed to verify the results.

The 6G-EWOC project addresses several key challenges in the development of 6G-V2X networks, including the need for high-speed, low-latency communication and advanced sensing capabilities. The project's focus on OWC technologies and AI-driven control and orchestration provides a promising approach to addressing these challenges. However, further analysis is needed to evaluate the project's potential impact and identify areas for improvement.
